statements.impact_statement: GHSA-9pwp-9qqc-pr26 is the GitHub Security Advisory alias for CVE-2026-8763, a Name Constraints bypass in Bouncy Castle for Java (bcprov/bcpkix before 1.85): a trailing dot in an rfc822Name or URI general name allows a certificate to evade name-constraint checks during X.509 path validation. Grype reports this finding under its GHSA identifier rather than the CVE, so a separate VEX statement is required alongside CVE-2026-8763.openvex.json. bcprov-jdk18on 1.84 is present in the Telicent images only as a transitive dependency of application libraries; the Bouncy Castle provider is not registered as the JSSE/X.509 trust provider and no Telicent code calls Bouncy Castle's certificate path validation. TLS handshakes and certificate chain validation in these images are performed by the JDK's default SunJSSE/SunPKIX providers, so the vulnerable name-constraint code is not in the execute path. Re-evaluate if Bouncy Castle is ever installed as the security provider or used for CertPath validation, and take bcprov-jdk18on 1.85 or later when the upstream dependency chain permits.
